title: Apply, she says
venue: the coast community-college paper, Newport · the laundromat digest
source: lore/drift_wood/_THE_COMPLETE_RUN.md (1999–2000 · deepening xix · the daily filled)
logline: A postcard from Seattle, the first. Four words legible among the tiny capitals: APPLY. YOU COWARD. — C. Wood reads it three times and pins it face out. Then face in.

panels.composition: Wood's bedroom. The corkboard: the crab flyer, the yearbook photo, a Timberline back page, the bus schedule. A postcard on the desk. WOOD.

image.prompt: a young man's bedroom with a corkboard pinned with a flyer, a yearbook photo, a newspaper page and a bus schedule, a postcard on the desk, black and white, no words
image.notes: Corkboard per objects.md 1998–99. The needle-tower postcard is Dec 20; this one is a ferry.

panels.composition: The postcard's back: tiny manic capitals edge to edge, and four words drawn legible in the middle.

image.prompt: close on a postcard's back covered edge to edge in tiny cramped handwriting with a few words larger in the middle, black and white, no words
image.notes: Letter after: APPLY. YOU COWARD. — C.

panels.composition: Wood pinning it to the corkboard, picture out: a ferry on gray water.

image.prompt: a young man pinning a postcard of a ferry on gray water to a corkboard, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The same pin. The card turned. Writing out. Then — his hand again — picture out. The strip leaves it there.

image.prompt: close on a hand turning a pinned postcard over on a corkboard and then back again, black and white, no words

art.line: brush-pen, committed; black and white; xerox

notes: 'APPLY. YOU COWARD.' The first postcard. Turned twice.
